whatChangedSinceCP1: The CP1 design said the readiness flip needed ZERO edits to src/tools.ts. That was WRONG, and the compiler caught it, not the plan.

cp1PredictionThatFailed.prediction: Flipping export_instrument to readiness 'blocked' requires no edit to artifacts/smartsite-mcp/src/tools.ts, because the readiness short-circuit runs before the switch.
cp1PredictionThatFailed.falsifier: npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit exits non-zero naming tools.ts
cp1PredictionThatFailed.outcome: FAILED. Verbatim: src/tools.ts(846,16): error TS2678: Type '"export_instrument"' is not comparable to type '"find_parcel" | "get_smart_site" | "list_my_properties" | "run_report" | "create_screen" | "add_to_screen" | "list_screens" | "save_property" | "set_property_status"'. Real exit code 2, captured with echo $? on the tsc invocation itself and not on a pipe (DEV_PROCESS 2.3).
cp1PredictionThatFailed.mechanism: registerTools returns early when readiness === 'blocked', so TypeScript narrows tool.name to the live names only. A handler case for a blocked tool then has a non-overlapping case label. This is the SAME forced-edit that CP1 correctly predicted for outright deletion; CP1 failed to see that the type narrowing makes the flip and the deletion identical from tools.ts's point of view.
cp1PredictionThatFailed.consequence: The minimum item 3 requires is a catalog line PLUS the removal of the export_instrument case from src/tools.ts. That crosses the dispatch's ring fence, so it is reported here explicitly rather than done quietly. The case block was replaced by a comment mirroring the ask_the_map precedent already in that file, and the rewire path is written into the comment.
cp1PredictionThatFailed.goodNews: The compiler enforcing this is itself the answer to half of item 4. A blocked tool that keeps a handler is a compile error; a live tool that loses its handler is a missing-return error. 'Typecheck' is a required status check on main. That invariant needed no new control.

secondFailureCaught.what: The first version of the item-4 control asserted, as its anti-vacuity guard, that src/tools.ts contains a hardcoded notReadyMessage("<name>") call site.
secondFailureCaught.howItSurfaced: After the tools.ts case was removed, that assertion failed: there are now ZERO hardcoded call sites, which is the FIXED state. Verbatim: AssertionError: expected 'import type { McpServer } from "@mode...' to match /function notReadyMessage\(/ (from the rename violation run) and, from the real run, the guard failing because no hardcoded call site remained.
secondFailureCaught.diagnosis: The guard was asserting that the DEFECT still exists. A control that requires its own defect to be present is a control that must be deleted the moment the defect is fixed. It also meant the predicate's negative-case fixture was reading live source that no longer carried the shape.
secondFailureCaught.fix: The defect text is now pinned as a verbatim fixture constant (P109_DEFECT_FIXTURE, copied from src/tools.ts at origin/main 91bfeed9), so the negative case survives the fix forever and does not depend on the defect remaining in the tree. The anti-vacuity guard now asserts only that the scanned file is the file the predicates were written against (notReadyMessage is defined, registerTools is defined, source is non-trivial) and that the case-label parser found at least 8 labels.
secondFailureCaught.secondPredicateAdded: handlerCaseLabels(source): live tools must equal the handler case labels inside registerTools only. Scoped to the slice after 'export function registerTools(' so inputSchemaFor's cases (which DO include blocked names like ask_the_map) cannot make it vacuous - and that scoping is itself asserted in a test.
